questions.q: Procurement costs often range between what share of an organisation's revenues?
questions.d: Procurement refers to raw materials, component parts and supplies bought from outside organisations to support operations. Procurement costs often range between 60% and 80% of an organisation's revenues.

questions.q: Which term is described as a relational exchange approach involving a limited number of suppliers?
questions.d: Supply management is viewed as a relational exchange approach involving a limited number of suppliers. Purchasing is the act of obtaining goods and services in exchange for money or its equivalent.

questions.q: In manual purchasing, which document becomes a binding contract once the supplier accepts it?
questions.d: The purchase order is the buyer's offer and becomes a binding contract when the supplier accepts it.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the three manual purchasing steps?
o: Purchase requisition → Request for quotation → Purchase order
Request for quotation → Purchase requisition → Purchase order
Purchase order → Request for quotation → Purchase requisition
Purchase requisition → Purchase order → Request for quotation
questions.d: Step 1: material/purchase requisition (product, quantity and due date). Step 2: the buyer identifies suppliers and issues a request for quotation. Step 3: the purchase order.

questions.q: In the e-procurement process, the buyer assigns qualified suppliers to bid when the purchase is over:
questions.d: e-Procurement: the user enters a purchase request, the requisition is approved and sent to the buyer, the buyer assigns qualified suppliers to bid if the purchase is over $50,000, then reviews closed bids and selects a supplier.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as an advantage of an e-procurement system?
questions.d: Advantages of e-procurement: time savings, cost savings, accuracy, real time, mobility, track ability, management, and benefits to the suppliers.

questions.q: A car maker buys the company that supplies its steel. This is:
questions.d: Backward integration means acquiring sources of supply. Forward integration means acquiring a customer's operations.

questions.q: A manufacturer buys the retail chain that sells its products. This is:
questions.d: Forward integration refers to acquiring a customer's operations. Backward integration refers to acquiring sources of supply.

questions.q: Which of these is a reason for MAKING an item in-house rather than buying it?
o: The firm is at or near capacity
The firm lacks the necessary expertise
The item is a non-vital component a supplier makes more cheaply
questions.d: Reasons for making: protect proprietary technology, no competent supplier, better quality control, use existing idle capacity, control of logistics, lower cost. Insufficient capacity, lack of expertise and cost advantage are reasons for buying.

questions.q: A restaurant buys ready-made desserts because its kitchen is already working at full capacity. Which reason for buying is this?
questions.d: Reasons for buying or outsourcing: cost advantage, insufficient capacity (the firm may be at or near capacity), lack of expertise, and quality.

questions.q: Which of these is a reason favouring MORE than one supplier?
o: Spreading the risk of supply interruption
The volume is too small to split
questions.d: Reasons for more than one supplier: need capacity, spread the risk of supply interruption, create competition, information, and dealing with special kinds of business. The other options are reasons favouring a single supplier.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as a supplier selection criterion?
o: The size of the supplier's advertising budget
Willingness to share technologies and information
questions.d: Supplier selection should use multiple criteria: product and process technologies, willingness to share technologies and information, quality, cost, reliability, order system and cycle time, capacity, communication capability, location and service.

questions.q: Which of these is an advantage of DECENTRALISED purchasing?
questions.d: Decentralisation advantages: closer knowledge of requirements, local sourcing, less bureaucracy. Concentrated volume, avoiding duplication, specialisation, lower transport costs, no competition within units and a common supply base are advantages of centralisation.

questions.q: How do the slides describe a hybrid purchasing organisation?
o: Decentralised at the corporate level and centralised at the business unit level
Centralised at the corporate level and decentralised at the business unit level
Fully outsourced to a third-party provider
questions.d: The slides describe a hybrid purchasing organisation as both decentralised at the corporate level and centralised at the business unit level.

questions.q: Which intermediary in international purchasing buys and takes title to the goods?
questions.d: Import broker or sales agent: performs a service for a fee. Import merchant: buys and takes title to the goods. Trading company: imports and carries a wide variety of goods.

questions.q: Supplier development (reverse marketing) means:
o: The purchaser takes the initiative, contacting suppliers and setting prices, terms and conditions
The supplier markets its products aggressively to the purchaser
The purchaser outsources all purchasing to a trading company
The purchaser and supplier merge through backward integration
questions.d: Reverse marketing is aggressive procurement involvement not typically part of supplier selection, such as the purchaser initiating contact with the supplier and establishing prices, terms and conditions.

questions.q: The slides describe single sourcing as a risky proposition.
questions.d: Single sourcing is a risky proposition. Although trends favour fewer sources, the slides advise avoiding a single source.

questions.q: 'Procurement' and 'purchasing' are never treated as the same thing.
questions.d: 'Procurement' and 'purchasing' are sometimes viewed as synonymous terms.

questions.q: Outsourcing means buying materials and components from suppliers instead of making them in-house, and the trend has moved away from outsourcing.
questions.d: Outsourcing is buying materials and components from suppliers instead of making them in-house, and the trend has moved toward outsourcing. The make-or-buy decision is strategic.

questions.q: Global sourcing requires additional skills and knowledge to deal with international suppliers, logistics, communication and the political environment.
questions.d: Global sourcing offers an opportunity to improve quality, cost and delivery performance, but requires additional skills and knowledge to deal with international suppliers, logistics, communication, the political environment and other issues.
